title: FLAMBE: A kinetic fluorescence polarization assay to study activation of monomeric BAX
protocol: Develop a fluorescence polarization assay for monitoring BAX early activation (FLAMBE).
Label the BAK-BH3 peptide with TAMRA to create BAKTAMRA.
Incubate BAKTAMRA with BAX to allow binding without activation of BAX.
Monitor an increase in Polarization over time as BAKTAMRA binds to BAX.
Observe a plateau in Polarization values as the maximum number of heterodimers form.
In samples showing BAX activation, note a release of BAKTAMRA and decrease in Polarization signal over time.
At any given time point, interpret the Polarization value to determine the fraction of activated BAX following dissociation.
Reconstitute TAMRA-labeled BAKBH3 peptide.
Monitor changes in Polarization as the BAX population binds to BAKTAMRA.
Observe an increase in Polarization if the entire population is heterodimeric.
Note a decrease in Polarization over time upon BAX activation due to displacement of BAKTAMRA.
Perform assays using a black 96-well microplate.
Include experimental samples without exceeding duplicates to avoid delays.
Ensure every experiment includes a BAKTAMRA control well.
Use a multi-channel pipette for serial dilution of BAX or titrant to reduce pipetting error across duplicates.
Utilize a PCR plate as a reagent reservoir to quickly add BAKTAMRA (or other components) to all wells.
Keep 0.5× PBS on ice.
Prepare assay reagents.
Prepare BAX.
Thaw a freezer stock of BAX protein on ice.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 10 s at 4°C to pellet large precipitates.
Pipette only soluble protein.
Pool aliquots into one tube before use.
Prepare 320 μL of a 500 nM (4×) working stock of BAX in 0.5× PBS.
Keep the BAX solution on ice.
Thaw a 2.2 μL aliquot of 0.5 mM BAKTAMRA on the benchtop or at 25°C.
Prepare a 1 μM master stock of BAKTAMRA by mixing 998 μL of 0.5× PBS with 2 μL of the 0.5 mM BAKTAMRA freezer stock.
Keep the BAKTAMRA solution on ice and protected from light.
Prepare a 200 nM working stock of BAKTAMRA by mixing 560 μL of 0.5× PBS and 140 μL of the 1 μM BAKTAMRA stock.
Keep the BAKTAMRA working stock on ice and protected from light.
Aliquot 150 μL of the 4× BAX stock into duplicate wells in row A.
Add 25 μL of 0.5× PBS to duplicate wells in rows B–H.
Prepare a 1.2× serial dilution of BAX in duplicate in the plate.
Using a multi-channel pipette, serially dilute BAX in 125 μL from row A to row G.
Discard the final 125 μL from row G to obtain a final volume of 25 μL per well.
Mix well by pipetting up and down several times before continuing to the next row.
Avoid generating bubbles during dilution.
Using a multi-channel pipette, add 50 μL of 0.5× PBS to all wells.
Quickly add 25 μL of the 200 nM BAKTAMRA working stock to all wells using a multi-channel pipette.
Proceed immediately to the next step after adding BAKTAMRA.
Aliquot BAKTAMRA into 8 wells of a PCR plate.
Maintain all reagents on ice before setting up the plate to minimize molecular interactions.
Load the prepared plate onto the tray and initiate the assay.
Save the exported file after assay completion.
Visualize kinetic data in GraphPad Prism or Microsoft Excel.
Keep 0.5× PBS on ice.
Prepare assay reagents.
In 0.5× PBS, prepare 450 μL of a BAX working stock that is 4× the non-activating concentration of BAX identified in the previous experiment and keep on ice.
Thaw BAX protein from the freezer stock used in the previous experiment or thaw a fresh tube if necessary.
Pool the thawed BAX protein for consistency.
Prepare a 200 nM working stock of BAKTAMRA by diluting 700 μL from the 1 μM master stock in 0.5× PBS.
Keep the BAKTAMRA working stock on ice and protected from light.
Store the BAKTAMRA master stock at 4°C for reuse within 1-2 days if protected from light.
Prepare a serial 2× dilution of BIMBH3 starting with a 30–50-fold molar excess relative to BAX.
Prepare 120 μL of a 4× stock of BIMBH3 in 0.5× PBS.
Aliquot 50 μL into duplicate wells in row A.
Add 25 μL of 0.5× PBS to all other titrant wells (rows B–F).
Mix well by pipetting up and down several times before continuing to the next row.
Serially dilute BIMBH3 in 25 μL from row A to F using a multi-channel pipette.
Discard the final 25 μL from row F to obtain the correct final volume of 25 μL.
Add 25 μL of 0.5× PBS to wells in rows A–F, 50 μL to row G, and 75 μL to row H using a multi-channel pipette.
Aliquot the 4× BAX stock in 7 wells of a PCR plate.
Using a multi-channel pipet, add 25 μL of BAX to rows A–G.
Each well will now contain 75 μL.
Initiate the FP protocol prior to adding BAKTAMRA.
Using a multi-channel pipette, add 25 μL of BAKTAMRA column-wise to all wells.
Immediately proceed to the next step after addition.
Aliquot 87.5 μL of BAKTAMRA into 8 wells of a PCR plate.
Load the plate onto the tray and initiate the assay by clicking "OK".
Save the exported file upon completion of the assay.
Visualize kinetic data in GraphPad Prism, Microsoft Excel, or similar program.
Keep 0.5× PBS on ice.
Prepare assay reagents.
In 0.5× PBS, prepare 700 μL of a BAX working stock that is 4× the non-activating concentration of BAX identified in the previous experiment and keep on ice.
Prepare a 700 μL working stock of BAKTAMRA at 200 nM in 0.5× PBS from the master stock.
Keep the BAKTAMRA working stock on ice and protected from light.
Prepare 700 μL of a 4× candidate ligand working stock in 0.5× PBS.
Prepare a 120 μL 4× stock of BIMBH3 in 0.5× PBS.
Aliquot 50 μL of the BIMBH3 stock into duplicate wells in row A.
Add 25 μL of 0.5× PBS to all titrant wells in rows B–H.
Serially dilute BIMBH3 from row A to H using a multi-channel pipette.
Discard the final 25 μL from row H.
Mix well by pipetting up and down several times before continuing to the next row.
Avoid generating bubbles during mixing.
Set up control wells in two consecutive wells of the third column with 50 μL of 0.5× PBS, followed by 25 μL of the 4× BAX working stock and 25 μL of BAKTAMRA for the BAX+BAKTAMRA control.

Set up another control in two consecutive wells of the third column with 25 μL of 0.5× PBS, followed by 25 μL of the 4× BAX working stock, 25 μL of the 4× ligand working stock, and 25 μL of BAKTAMRA for the BAX+Ligand+BAKTAMRA control.
Set up the BAKTAMRA control in two consecutive wells of the third column with 75 μL of 0.5× PBS followed by 25 μL of the 200 nM BAKTAMRA stock.
Divide the remaining 650 μL of 4× ligand working stock in 8 wells of a PCR plate.
Using a multi-channel pipette, aliquot 25 μl per well in all titrant wells.
Divide 600 μL of 4× BAX working stock into 8 wells of a PCR plate.
Add 25 μL per well to all titrant wells using a multi-channel pipette.
Divide the remaining 550 μL of the 200 nM BAKTAMRA working stock into 8 wells of a PCR plate.
Add 25 μL of BAKTAMRA to all titrant wells using a multi-channel pipette.
Load the plate onto the tray.
Initiate the assay by clicking "OK".
Run the assay for 1 hour.
Save the exported file after assay completion.
Visualize kinetic data in GraphPad Prism, Microsoft Excel, or a similar program.
